_comment_s104: S104 (2026-08-12) added ignore glob '*/rebuild/dist/*'. RATIONALE, stated openly because narrowing MCV scope silently is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent: rebuild/dist is esbuild+asset BUILD OUTPUT, is listed in rebuild/.gitignore, and is regenerated byte-identically by `npm run build` from sources that ARE diff-bound (src/**, tools/**). Asserting on it would bind claims to artefacts rather than to authored code. This exactly mirrors the pre-existing '*/public/dist/*' entry for the frozen old build. The SOURCES of those artefacts (tools/build-atlas.py, tools/build-player.py, src/art/*) remain diff-bound and carry content assertions in S104 P2.

Scopes diff-binding to THIS project's agent-authored surfaces; the global config's WS1 toolkit roots (~/.claude/scripts|hooks|skills, parent-workspace plans/boot-snapshot) belong to parent-workspace sessions and were tripping cross-session false-positive UNBOUND fails here (8 on 2026-07-17, all S176 DB-durability work from another seat). _comment_s105: S105 (2026-08-12) added ignore glob '*/rebuild/realm/realm.db'. RATIONALE, stated openly because narrowing MCV scope silently is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent: realm.db is a DERIVED INDEX, listed in rebuild/.gitignore, deleted and rebuilt from scratch by `npm run realm:build` out of realm/*.json -- and every one of those seven JSON sources IS diff-bound and carries content assertions in S105 P1/P2. Asserting on the .db would bind claims to an artefact rather than to authored data. This mirrors the existing '*/rebuild/dist/*' and '*/public/dist/*' entries exactly. The realm/*.json sources remain diff-bound.
_comment_s106: S106 (2026-08-13) added ignore globs '*/rebuild/docs/renders/*', '*/rebuild/realm/realm.db-shm' and '*/rebuild/realm/realm.db-wal'. RATIONALE, stated openly because narrowing MCV scope silently is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent, and this session already added 46 files under docs/renders alone: (a) docs/renders/** is PURE BUILD OUTPUT of tools/render-map.py, tools/render-views.py and tools/build-atlas.py - deterministic PNGs regenerated byte-identically from sources that ARE diff-bound and DO carry content assertions in S106 P1/P2. Asserting on them would bind claims to artefacts rather than to authored code, which is precisely the objection recorded for '*/rebuild/dist/*' in S104. (b) realm.db-shm / realm.db-wal are SQLite's shared-memory and write-ahead-log sidecars for realm.db, which is ALREADY ignored; they are transient, byte-unstable between runs, and carry no authored content. The realm SOURCE (realm/*.json) stays bound and is asserted record-by-record in S106 P4.
_comment_s110: S110: docs/s110-film/ holds GENERATED AI MEDIA (Imagen plates, Veo clips, the stitched film) produced for the cinematic. Only the BINARIES are ignored, on the same basis as docs/renders/* above: MCV diff-binding asserts text content, and there is nothing meaningful it can assert about a generated PNG. The narrow globs are deliberate — docs/s110-film/PLATES.md stays diff-bound, because the prompts, the model used and the honest gap-list ARE checkable text and are the part that must not drift. _comment_s116: S116 (2026-08-21) added ignore glob '*/rebuild/docs/shots/*'. RATIONALE, stated openly because narrowing MCV scope silently is exactly what this mechanism exists to prevent, and this session alone put 16 files there: docs/shots/** is CAPTURED FRAMES from tools/shoot.ts — PNGs read back out of the running game's WebGL buffer, listed in rebuild/.gitignore, and regenerable in seconds by re-running the harness. There is nothing meaningful MCV can assert about a screenshot; asserting on them would bind claims to artefacts rather than to authored code, which is precisely the objection already recorded for '*/rebuild/dist/*' (S104), '*/rebuild/docs/renders/*' (S106) and the generated media under docs/s110-film (S110). THE SOURCES STAY BOUND AND ARE ASSERTED: tools/shoot.ts and tools/shot-inspect.py both carry content assertions in S116 P1 (20 of them, including the readback mechanism, the CORS header, the mousemove-not-pointermove trap, the instrument check, and the exact-per-channel diff that replaced a byte-length comparison), and docs/SEEING-THE-GAME.md — the procedure and the traps, which IS checkable text and is the part that must not drift — is deliberately NOT ignored and carries three assertions of its own. The frames themselves are verified the only way an image can be: by Daniel looking at them.
